newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen selling off at start.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen selling off at start.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open lower Thursday, following through on yesterday's downward momentum.
The four stocks being dropped from the Dow Jones Industrial Average effective March 17 are likely to decline, while their replacements are poised to move higher, analysts said.
"There will be four losers and four winners," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities. "Dow index fund players will be buying the four new additions."
Texaco Inc, Bethlehem Steel Corp, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Woolworth Corp are being dropped from the blue-chip index.
Being added are Hewlett-Packard Co, Johnson & Johnson , Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Travelers Group Inc.

"There is the momentum of the prior session to take into account in gauging the open," Wachtel said. "The prior session in this case was choppy, weak. The problem is the transition of the market's leadership. People are tired of consumer and financial stocks. And techs are taking a beating."
He said interest was shifting to such economically sensitive sectors as retailers and airlines.

"We sense that there is a rising rate structure coming, and people are also making adjustments because the upcoming quarter will be less aggressive," Wachtel said. "These are the things weighing on the market."
He said declines in the four stocks being ousted from the Dow would not have a decisive influence on the index.
"They may take two or three points off the Dow," he said.
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average was down 282.79 points, or 1.56 percent, at 17,900.48.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was down 13 points at 4409.5.
The shuffle in the Dow stocks was the main influence on a mixed U.S. shares trading session in London.
Texaco was down 1-1/4 at 101-1/2, Bethlehem Steel fell 1/4 to 8-1/2, Westinghouse fell 3/8 to 18-5/8, and Woolworth was down 1/4 at 22-3/4.
Hewlett-Packard climbed 3/8 to 55 and Johnson and Johnson gained 3/8 to 60.

General Motors Corp fell 3/8 to 57-3/8 after releasing a financial breakdown of its auto-building operations and its Delphi auto parts unit, in preparation for the sale of 20 percent of Delphi. Other motor shares came off in sympathy, with Ford Motor Co falling 1/4 to 32-1/2 and Chrysler Corp 1/4 weaker at 31-1/8.
The dollar was mixed in Tokyo and stalled in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were unchanged to lower, with the long bond off 4/32 to yield 6.89 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said one reason for the rally in tobacco shares is mounting speculation that a "magic bullet" legislative solution will wipe away the regulatory and legal attacks dogging cigarette makers and depressing their share prices.
